transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I’m having trouble with heights at work. Scaffolds, roof edges, upper platforms… even when I can see the rails are there, my mind just keeps telling me I’m about to go over. It’s gotten hard to be near them.
Does this fear happen only when you’re up high or near an edge?

Yeah… mostly when I’m up high or right near an edge. Scaffolds, roof edges, upper platforms — even if the rails are there and I know it’s supposed to be safe, my head still tells me I’m going to go over.
Outside of being up high or near an edge, do you have the same kind of intense fear in other situations?
No… not really. It’s mainly when I’m near scaffolds, roof edges, upper platforms — that kind of thing. Even if the rails are there, I still get this feeling like I’m about to go over.
When you’re up high or near an edge, do you ever suddenly get a full panic attack?

Yeah… I don’t know if I’d call it a full panic attack, but it hits fast. The second I step onto temporary stairs or start toward an open upper floor, my chest tightens, my hands get sweaty, and my legs feel like they might lock up. Then it’s hard to make myself keep moving.
Have you ever had one of these sudden attacks when you were not up high or near an edge?
Not that I can think of… no. It’s pretty tied to being up high or close to an edge.
